description: An operations manager must authorize a weekend run of Assembly Cell 8 and finalize the operator roster, maintenance stop, and quality-release controls for a 480-unit pump-housing order.

shared_context.S1: Assembly Cell 8 is available for weekend production of 480 pump housings.
shared_context.S2: The standard weekend plan uses one Saturday shift and one Sunday shift, each lasting up to 8 hours.
shared_context.S3: Each shift normally has two operators, and the operations manager must approve the final weekend plan.
shared_context.S4: During the pre-overtime huddle, workforce coordination, maintenance, and quality each report relevant constraints before the roster and production controls are locked.

PF1.text: The current certification matrix shows that Saturday's Cell 8 roster must be Lina, who is setup-certified, and Sam, who is run-certified; Sunday's roster must be Ruth, who is setup-certified, and Omar, who is run-certified. Elias checked the matrix after the last training audit, but the updated roster has not yet been attached to the weekend work order.

PF2.text: Mei's inspection found that Cell 8's conveyor servo requires a 90-minute preventive inspection between the Saturday and Sunday shifts; she recorded the finding in her maintenance notebook during the morning walkaround, but has not entered it in the electronic work order.

PF3.text: The customer quality amendment requires 12 first-off units after the weekend setup and 100% torque verification on the first 30 units after the maintenance restart, with quality signoff before the remaining units are released. Caleb received the signed amendment by email, but it has not yet been linked to the order record.

acceptance_conditions: The weekend run must be authorized for all 480 units.
Saturday must use Lina and Sam, and Sunday must use Ruth and Omar.
A 90-minute maintenance inspection must be scheduled between the shifts.
Twelve first-off units must be produced after setup.
The first 30 units after the maintenance restart must receive 100% torque verification.
Quality signoff must be required before the remaining units are released.
A maintenance work-order commitment and a quality-release commitment must be recorded.
The customer quality amendment must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C2: decisions['saturday_operator_1'] == 'Lina' and decisions['saturday_operator_2'] == 'Sam' and decisions['sunday_operator_1'] == 'Ruth' and decisions['sunday_operator_2'] == 'Omar'
content_checks.C7: any(c.get('target') in ['Mei', 'A3'] and '90-minute' in c.get('detail', '') and 'conveyor servo' in c.get('detail', '') and ('electronic work order' in c.get('detail', '') or 'work order' in c.get('detail', '')) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any(c.get('target') in ['Caleb', 'A4'] and ('signed customer quality amendment' in c.get('detail', '') or 'signed amendment' in c.get('detail', '')) and ('quality signoff' in c.get('detail', '') or 'quality gate' in c.get('detail', '')) and ('order record' in c.get('detail', '') or 'remaining units' in c.get('detail', '')) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The certification matrix changes the four operator assignments from a generic two-person-per-shift roster to Saturday Lina and Sam and Sunday Ruth and Omar.
The servo finding changes the inter-shift maintenance stop from no specified outage to exactly 90 minutes and requires a maintenance work-order commitment.
The signed amendment changes release controls to exactly 12 first-off units, 100% torque verification on exactly 30 restart units, mandatory quality signoff, and a quality-release commitment.
